info.name: VibeZone API
description: VibeZone REST API v1 for native apps (Flutter) — see docs/api/README.md and docs/adr/0007-native-app-token-auth.md.
Quick start (local Docker stack, `docker compose --profile app up -d`):
1. Set the collection variables `email`, `password`, `handle` (or keep the defaults).
2. Auth (app) → Register → "DEV: read verification email (Mailpit)" → Verify email → Sign in (token).
3. Every other request then sends `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}` (collection auth).
The collection pre-request script refreshes the access token automatically when it is about to expire.
- Access token: 15 min. On 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"` → refresh once, retry.
- Refresh token: single use, rotates every refresh. Run at most ONE refresh at a time (single-flight);
reusing an old refresh token signs the device out. On 401 `invalid_refresh_token` → go to the login screen.
- Store the refresh token in secure storage (flutter_secure_storage). Never log tokens.
- Errors are RFC 9457 Problem Details with a stable `code` (and `errors[field] = [code]` for validation).
- Bearer requests need no CSRF token. Cookie/CSRF requests in the "Web (cookie) only" folder are for browsers.

exec: // Auto-refresh: if the access token expires within 30 s and we have a refresh token, rotate first.
body: { mode: "raw", raw: JSON.stringify({ refreshToken: refresh }) },
console.warn("Refresh failed — sign in again", err || res.code);

item.name: Auth (app)
item.description: Account + token endpoints. No cookies, no CSRF.

request.description: 202 for any valid input (anti-enumeration): a verification email — or an 'account exists' email — follows. handle: 3–30 chars a-z 0-9 _ -; password ≥ 10 chars; locale vi|en.

exec: // The Postman sandbox has no URL global: read the query values with a regex.
const param = (name) => { const m = link.match(new RegExp("[?&]" + name + "=([^&\\s]+)")); return m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : ""; };

request.description: Local development helper only: finds the newest email to {{email}} in Mailpit and stores userId + token. In the app the user taps the link in the email (https://<web>/{locale}/verify-email?userId=…&token=…) — handle it as a deep link and call Verify email.
204. Idempotent. 400 token_invalid.
Always 202.

200 → {data: {accessToken, tokenType: 'Bearer', expiresIn: 900, refreshToken, refreshTokenExpiresAt}}. 401 invalid_credentials (wrong email/password or locked out — indistinguishable). 403 email_not_confirmed. 429 too many attempts. deviceName is shown in the signed-in devices list.
Returns a NEW pair; the old refresh token stops working. 401 invalid_refresh_token → sign in again. Never run two refreshes in parallel.
204, idempotent. Ends the session; the access token stops working within seconds. Then delete both tokens on the device.
Alternative sign-out using the access token. 204, idempotent.
Always 202. The email links to https://<web>/{locale}/reset-password?email=…&token=… (1 h). Use the Mailpit helper above to grab resetToken locally.
204. Signs out ALL sessions (web and app). 400 token_invalid, password_too_short, password_too_long.
data: {id, email, handle, displayName, locale, emailConfirmed, roles[], avatar: {small, large} | null}. 401 when not signed in.
204. Signs out every OTHER session (including other app devices); this one stays valid.
data[]: {id, createdAt, lastSeenAt, userAgent (deviceName for apps), isCurrent}; meta {page, pageSize, total, hasMore}.
204; 404 session_not_found.
200 {data: {revoked: n}}.

Any signed-in user (not only artists). Raw body = the image (JPEG/PNG/WebP, ≥ 200×200 px, ≤ 10 MB); cropped square, metadata removed. 200 → data: {small, large} URLs (also in Me.avatar). Errors: image_invalid, image_too_small, image_too_large. Rate limit: 30/hour per IP.
image/jpeg, public. 'small' or 'large'. Prefer the URLs in Me.avatar / playlist owner (they change when the picture changes). 404 without a picture.
204, idempotent.
Public reference data: data[] {slug, name}, meta.
Public, ready tracks, newest first. data[] + meta {page, pageSize, total, hasMore}; load the next page while hasMore.
Public/unlisted tracks for everyone; private/processing tracks only for the owner (else 404). Includes status, durationMs, playable.
Artist profile + public tracks. 404 if unknown.
404 if the user has not created one yet. data.avatar / data.banner = {small, large} URLs or null.
201. Grants the Artist role (needed to create tracks). 409 if the slug is taken or the user already has one.
The artist's own tracks, any status, newest first (paged).
201 → track in status Draft (no audio). Prefer Media → 'Upload a new track', which does it in one request. visibility: Public | Unlisted | Private. 403 if the user is not an artist.
Owner only (others get 404). Send the full object.
204. Owner only.
Artist only. kind: Album | Ep | Single; visibility: Public | Unlisted | Private. 201 → data: AlbumDto.
Album + tracks the viewer can see, in order. Cover = its first track cover. Private: owner only (404).
Owner only. The complete tracklist in order (your own tracks, ≤ 100). Tracks left out leave the album.
Owner only. Send the full object.
The signed-in artist's albums (any visibility).
204. Tracks are kept.
Top 6 tracks, artists and albums with totals. Accent-insensitive ("son tung" finds "Sơn Tùng"), prefix and typo tolerant. Only listed content (Ready public tracks, public albums).
Paged: data[] TrackDto + meta {page, pageSize, total, hasMore}.
Paged: data[] ArtistDto.
Paged: data[] AlbumDto (public albums only).
Public playlists with tracks; without q: newest first.
Any signed-in user. visibility: Public | Private. 201 → data: PlaylistDto.
Owner only; any track you can see. Already there → no-op. 400 playlist_full at 500.
Private: owner only (404). coverUrls = up to 4 track covers for a mosaic.
In order, without tracks the viewer can't see.
Owner only. The tracks you see, in their new order; they swap among their current positions (hidden tracks keep theirs).
Recently updated first (paged).
Owner only. Send the full object.

item.name: Upload a new track (details + audio + cover)

request.description:
One request creates the track and starts processing — all or nothing (on any error no track exists).
multipart/form-data with text fields first, then artwork (optional), then audio. 202 → data: upload status; Location: /api/v1/tracks/{id}.
Errors (400, field in errors): track_title_invalid, track_description_too_long, track_visibility_invalid, genre_unknown, audio_required, unsupported_file_type, file_too_large, artwork_invalid, artwork_too_small, artwork_too_large; multipart_required / multipart_invalid; 403 artist_required.
Flutter (dio): FormData.fromMap({'title': …, 'visibility': 'Public', 'artwork': await MultipartFile.fromFile(coverPath), 'audio': await MultipartFile.fromFile(path)}) with onSendProgress.
Rate limit: 30 uploads/hour per IP.
Owner only. Raw body = the image (JPEG/PNG/WebP, ≥ 200×200 px, ≤ 10 MB). 200 → data: {small, large} URLs. Cropped to a square; metadata removed.
204. Owner only.
image/jpeg. 'small' (≈320 px) or 'large' (≈1200 px). Use the URLs in track.artwork (they change when the cover changes). Anyone who can see the track; 404 otherwise or without a cover.
Signed-in artist. Raw body = image (JPEG/PNG/WebP, ≥ 200×200, ≤ 10 MB); cropped square. 200 → data: {small, large}. Errors: image_invalid, image_too_small, image_too_large; 404 artist_not_found.
Like the avatar, but 3:1 (≥ 600×200). 800/1600 px wide renditions.
image/jpeg, public. /avatar/{small|large} or /banner/{small|large}. Prefer the URLs in ArtistDto.avatar / banner. 404 without an image.

For an existing Draft, or again after Failed/Cancelled — new tracks use "Upload a new track". Raw request body = the audio file (NOT multipart). Pick the file under Body → binary and set {{uploadLength}} to its size in bytes.
MP3/WAV/FLAC/AAC/M4A/OGG/Opus, ≤ 200 MB, 1 s–2 h. 202 → processing starts (track status Processing → Ready/Failed).
Errors: upload_length_required, file_too_large, upload_incomplete (size mismatch / connection dropped), unsupported_file_type, track_not_uploadable / upload_in_progress (409). Processing failures (unsupported_format, no_audio_stream, duration_too_short|long, processing_*) appear in track.processingError.
Flutter (dio): dio.put(url, data: file.openRead(), options: Options(headers: {'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream', 'X-Upload-Length': await file.length(), 'X-File-Name': Uri.encodeComponent(name)}), onSendProgress: …).
Rate limit: 30 uploads/hour per IP.
Owner only: status (Uploaded / Processing / Completed / Failed / Cancelled), attempts, error code. Poll every 2–5 s, or poll the track.
204 while queued/processing; 409 if already finished.

200 → data: {trackId, streamUrl, waveformUrl, contentType: "audio/mp4", sizeBytes, durationMs, expiresAt}. Cache-Control: no-store.
streamUrl/waveformUrl are relative to the base URL and carry ?token=vzp_… (valid ~6 h): hand baseUrl + streamUrl to the player with NO headers
(just_audio: AudioSource.uri(Uri.parse(baseUrl + streamUrl)) — works with background playback, iOS, casting).
Public tracks: works without sign-in. Private tracks: owner only (bearer). 404 track_not_found / media_not_ready.
When the player gets 401 playback_token_invalid (expired), call this endpoint again and resume at the same position.
What the player requests: the URL from "Playback URLs", no Authorization header. AAC (audio/mp4), HTTP Range. 401 playback_token_invalid when expired.
Same stream authorised by bearer/cookie instead of a token (the web app uses this). Public tracks need no auth. 404 when not visible or not ready.
data: {version, durationMs, peaks: float[~1000] in 0..1}. Same visibility rules as streaming; also accepts ?token= (use waveformUrl).

item.name: Social
item.description: Likes, follows and timed comments (M4). Writes are rate-limited (60/min per account).

request.description: data: {likeCount, commentCount, liked}. Anyone who can see the track (liked=false when signed out).
Idempotent. Track must be playable for you. 200 → engagement. The artist gets a notification (not for their own tracks).
Idempotent. 200 → engagement.
All ids (≤ 5000, newest first) — mark hearts in lists without one request per track.
Top-level comments newest first (paged); each has replies[] oldest first. timestampMs = moment of the track (ms) or null. Plain text — render as text.

1–1000 chars. timestampMs pins it to the waveform (top-level only). parentId → reply (a reply to a reply attaches to its top-level comment). 201. Errors: comment_body_invalid, comment_timestamp_invalid, comment_not_found (parent).
Author only (404 otherwise).
204. Author, the track's owner or a moderator; 404 for others.
data: {followerCount, following}.
Idempotent. 400 follow_self for your own profile. The artist gets a notification.
Idempotent.
data: [{likedAt, track: TrackDto}], newest like first. Tracks you can no longer see are left out (total still counts them).
Recently played: [{playedAt, track}], one entry per track, most recent first.
[{id, slug, name, avatarUrl, followedAt}] newest first (paged).
Chart: valid listens + 2 × likes over the last 7 days, recent days weigh more. Same for everyone (not personalised). Top 100, paged.
≤ 12 public tracks by the same artist or in the same genre (label them as such in the UI — not recommendations).
data: {plays (started), listens (valid)}, all time.

Send from the player: "started" when a track starts (new sessionId per start), "progress" every ~15 s of actual listening, "completed" at the end.
listenedMs = playback time accumulated in this session (seeks don't count); the server caps it by wall-clock time since the session started.
A valid listen = ≥ 30 s (half of tracks under 60 s), once per listener and track per 30 minutes. Event ids are idempotency keys: retry a failed batch with the same ids.
Signed-out players may send clientId (a random UUID kept on the device) so their listens de-duplicate. 1–50 events per batch; 202 → {accepted}. Rate limit 60 batches/min.

item.name: Notifications
item.description: Realtime: SignalR hub {{baseUrl}}/api/v1/hubs/notifications (apps: ?access_token={{accessToken}}) sends 'unread' with {count}; then refetch.

request.description: Newest first. type: TrackLiked, ArtistFollowed, CommentPosted, CommentReplied, TrackReady, TrackFailed, ReportResolved, ContentRemoved. Link with trackId / artistSlug; code = error/outcome/reason.
data: {count}.
204; 404 if it isn't yours.

subjectType: Track | Comment | Playlist; reason: Copyright | Abuse | Spam | Other. 201. Errors: report_own_content (400), report_subject_not_found (404), report_exists (409 — one open report per item).
Moderator/Admin. status=Open (oldest first) | Actioned | Rejected; omit for all. 403 for other users.
Moderator/Admin. action: remove (takes the content down and settles every open report on it) | dismiss. Audited; reporters and the owner are notified. 409 report_not_open.
Moderator/Admin. Track or Playlist. 204. Audited.
Moderator or Admin. Idempotent, audited, effective immediately.
400 role_self_admin when removing your own Admin.
Moderators too. Every non-deleted track, any status/visibility.
{pending, deadLettered, processedLastDay}.

item.name: Web (cookie) only
item.description: Browser flow, for reference. Apps should use the token endpoints instead. Postman keeps the cookies automatically.

request.description: 204 + session cookie. Fetch a new CSRF token afterwards (tokens are bound to the identity).
Only reachable on the API port (5080) — the proxy routes /api only.
